stories.headline: Russian missile and drone barrage strikes Kyiv, killing at least 16 and injuring dozens
stories.body:
Russian forces launched a heavy missile and drone attack on Kyiv overnight into Thursday, causing widespread destruction and multiple casualties. Official reports presented differing numbers for the casualties across the capital. Kyiv officials reported that at least 16 people were killed in and around the city, while the State Emergency Service of Ukraine reported that at least 17 people were killed across Kyiv. Official sources also reported different figures for the number of injured people. Authorities reported that 33 people were injured in Kyiv, whereas the State Emergency Service of Ukraine reported that more than 40 people were injured across the capital.

The aerial attack hit several civilian locations. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko stated that homes, a school, and a children's medical center were damaged in the attack. Specific neighborhoods suffered severe losses, with eight people reported killed in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district during the attack. Outside the main city, Tymur Tkachenko, governor of the Kyiv region, said a strike in Brovary district killed one man and wounded another.

Ukraine's air force provided details regarding the scale of the Russian bombardment. The air force reported that Russia launched 168 drones alongside dozens of ballistic, cruise, and hypersonic missiles. Air defense forces managed to intercept many incoming weapons. Ukraine's air force reported shooting down 41 out of 46 cruise missiles and 145 drones launched by Russia. However, defense systems could not halt every threat. Ukraine's air force stated that none of the high-speed ballistic missiles launched by Russia were intercepted. To counter these weapons, Ukraine relies on American supplies of Patriot interceptor missiles to defend against Russian ballistic missiles.

The attack also created international effects. Romania's defence ministry stated a drone entered Romanian airspace near Galați and crashed in Tulcea county. Across the border, Russia's defence ministry claimed that 726 Ukrainian drones were shot down over various regions in Russia.

stories.headline: United States plans heavy economic campaign against Iran following military conflict
stories.body:
The United States has announced plans for major economic measures intended to collapse the Iranian regime. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC that the US would apply the toughest sanctions in history on Iran, with further details of the plan to be announced on August 24. US President Donald Trump warned that any country providing a lifeline to Iran will face tremendous economic consequences. Expanding measures against Iran's allies, the US administration designated 10 people associated with Hezbollah, including a Turkish businessman.

These economic actions follow recent military hostilies. The US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February. The US and Iran later agreed to ceasefires in April and June to facilitate negotiations to end the conflict.

Iranian officials strongly condemned the US announcements. Iran's foreign ministry characterized US economic sanctions as 'economic terrorism' and 'crimes against humanity'. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated US economic threats aim to divert US public attention from domestic financial problems. On maritime control, Iranian consul general in Mumbai Saeid Reza Mosayeb Motlagh rejected Donald Trump's claim that the US has total control over the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the US fulfills commitments under a Memorandum of Understanding. Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates suspended all trade activities and financial transactions with Iran after detecting two missiles launched from the country. Prior to the war, the United Arab Emirates provided more than 30% of Iran's imports.

stories.headline: Chinese court sentences Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan to life in prison
stories.body:
The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court has sentenced Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan to life in prison and confiscated all of his personal property. Hui Ka Yan pleaded guilty in April to eight charges including misuse of funds, fundraising fraud, and bribery. In March 2024, Hui Ka Yan was fined $6.5 million and banned for life from China's capital market.

The court also levied heavy fines against the corporation, fining Evergrande Group 8.8 billion yuan and its property arm 7 billion yuan. Regulators in Hong Kong and mainland Chinese authorities found Evergrande overstated revenues by roughly $80 billion over 2019 and 2020. Evergrande defaulted on most of its $300 billion in liabilities after the Chinese government introduced regulations limiting developer debt in 2020.

Legal penalties reached dozens of other company officials. More than 50 individuals linked to Evergrande were sentenced on Thursday, receiving prison terms ranging from 20 months to 18 years. Hui Ka Yan's sons, Xu Zhijian and Xu Tenghe, were among the Evergrande executives sentenced to jail terms ranging from 22 months to 18 years.

stories.headline: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected President of Bangladesh in historic vote
stories.body:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected President of Bangladesh after defeating challenger Oli Ahmed by 255 votes to 88. Out of 349 registered voting lawmakers, 343 participated in the parliamentary vote. This election marked the first contested presidential vote in Bangladesh since 1991. Alamgir will take office as Bangladesh's 23rd President.

Alamgir previously served as secretary-general of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party. The presidential vote occurred after former Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned halfway through his term last month. Parliamentary Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad served as acting president following Shahabuddin's resignation.

The political transition comes during legal proceedings against former leaders. Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was sentenced to be hanged after being found guilty in absentia of crimes against humanity.

stories.headline: Jailed former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan transferred to hospital
stories.body:
Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was transferred from Adiala jail to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad under heavy security. The movement followed an order from a three-judge panel of Pakistan's Supreme Court requiring that Imran Khan be taken to a hospital within 48 hours for a medical examination.

Imran Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 on corruption charges. His health condition has caused concern; in February, Imran Khan's lawyer stated he had only 15% vision left in his right eye. Imran Khan's next court hearing is scheduled for September 16, and his lawyer stated he should remain hospitalized until at least then.

Government ministers committed to respecting the judicial order. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry affirmed the Pakistani government would fully comply with the Supreme Court ruling regarding Imran Khan. Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry stated the government could consider medical treatment abroad for Imran Khan if adequate care was unavailable domestically.

stories.headline: North Korea fires short-range ballistic missiles following US drill cutbacks
stories.body:
North Korea launched about 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward its eastern waters on Thursday. South Korea's military reported the missiles were launched from the Pyongyang area at around 5pm (08.00 GMT).

The missile firings took place after the US and South Korea scaled back their 11-day Ulchi Freedom Shield military exercises following orders from Donald Trump. Donald Trump cited his relationship with Kim Jong-un and South Korea's refusal to support the US war against Iran as reasons for scaling back military drills. Donald Trump told reporters on Wednesday that he would be meeting Kim Jong-un later this year.

However, North Korean officials dismissed the significance of the US changes. Kim Yo-jong dismissed Trump's reduction of joint military exercises, stating the aggressive nature of the drills remained unchanged. Kim Yo-jong also denied Donald Trump's assertion that Kim Jong-un had responded to a request for a conversation.

stories.headline: Israeli military admits shooting at car carrying child in Gaza and opens probes
stories.body:
The Israeli military admitted its troops opened fire in 2024 on a car in Gaza carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab and six family members. Research agencies Forensics Architecture and Earshot mapped 335 bullet holes on the car carrying Hind Rajab. The Israeli military also admitted its troops fired on a Red Crescent ambulance dispatched to rescue Hind Rajab, killing two medics. Following these statements, the Israeli military announced a criminal investigation by its military police into the killing of Hind Rajab and her family.

In addition, the Israeli military initiated a criminal investigation into the March 2025 killing of 15 Palestinian medics and humanitarian personnel near Rafah. Israeli troops had bulldozed the bodies and emergency vehicles of the 15 killed personnel into a mass grave near Rafah. However, the Israeli military decided against opening a criminal investigation into the April 2024 airstrikes that killed seven World Central Kitchen aid workers.

Overall, the Health Ministry in Gaza reported that more than 73,000 people have been killed in Gaza during Israel's military campaign.

stories.headline: Jharkhand High Court stays order cancelling state civil service appointments
stories.body:
The Jharkhand High Court stayed state government notifications cancelling appointments made through the 11th and 13th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) examinations. Justice Deepak Roshan of the High Court issued the order, allowing affected employees selected through the 11th and 13th JPSC exams to continue holding their positions while petitions are heard. Justice Deepak Roshan directed the state government to file its reply by September 15.

The court order comes after state-wide government actions regarding examination irregularities. On August 18, the Jharkhand government cancelled 22 examinations and ordered a probe into 23 others conducted since 2014. Three members of the Jharkhand Public Service Commission have resigned following examination irregularity allegations. Furthermore, a petition was filed in the Supreme Court of India seeking a CBI investigation into alleged malpractices in the JPSC Preliminary Examination.

Public anger over the issue remains high. Protesting student leaders announced plans to burn effigies of Chief Minister Hemant Soren across all 24 districts of Jharkhand.

stories.headline: Supreme Court holds 1978 landmark definition of industry applies to pending labor disputes
stories.body:
A nine-judge Supreme Court bench ruled that pending labor disputes under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, will continue to be decided based on a landmark 1978 judgment. At the same time, the nine-judge bench held that the 1978 Bangalore Water Supply judgment's definition of 'industry' will not apply to Section 2(p) of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant authored the majority opinion for the nine-judge bench. The ruling addresses how legal standards function alongside newer statutory frameworks. The Industrial Relations Code, 2020, came into force on November 21, 2025.

The 1978 Bangalore Water Supply decision defined legal standards for workplaces through three specific conditions. The 1978 triple test for defining an industry requires systematic activity, functional cooperation between employer and employees, and production of goods or services. Under the court's decision, this triple test remains the governing standard for resolving all pending disputes filed under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

The ruling was not unanimous. Justice B.V. Nagarathna, joined by Justices Dipankar Datta and Ujjal Bhuyan, dissented. In their dissenting opinion, the judges held that reconsidering the 1978 judgment was unwarranted.

stories.headline: India permits duty-free raw sugar imports to help reduce rising domestic prices
stories.body:
The Indian government has allowed duty-free imports of 10 lakh (1 million) tonnes of raw sugar for the first time in a decade. The Directorate General of Foreign Trade set October 31, 2026, as the deadline for duty-free raw sugar imports under the Tariff Rate Quota.

The decision comes after domestic sugar prices rose significantly. Average retail sugar prices in India reached Rs 52.3 per kg, representing a 13% increase from a year earlier. Similarly, the all-India average ex-mill sugar price rose to Rs 5,400-5,500 per quintal, up from Rs 3,900 a year earlier.

In addition to allowing imports, the government placed limits on major domestic buyers. The food ministry capped sugar inventories for bulk consumers using over 10 tonnes a month to a maximum of 15 days of consumption. The stockholding restrictions for bulk sugar consumers will apply from September 1 to November 30.

stories.headline: Supreme Court creates five-member panel to probe police action during student march
stories.body:
The Supreme Court formed a five-member high-powered enquiry committee led by retired judge R Subhash Reddy to probe police actions during a July 20 student protest march to Parliament. The enquiry committee members include former CJ Ravi S Jha, former judge Shalinder Kaur, former CBI director Rishi Kumar Shukla, and former DGP LR Bishnoi.

The July 20 demonstrations resulted in widespread injuries. Delhi Police reported in an affidavit that 248 police personnel and 218 protesters were injured during the July 20 demonstrations. The student protests were organized by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) against alleged paper leaks in national examinations.

The protests triggered political resignations and public demonstrations. Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down from his position as Union Education Minister on July 25 following paper leak protests. Additionally, climate activist Sonam Wangchuk ended a 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital after demonstrating in solidarity with CJP.
